description:
Found by the reviewing session at the s540c merge review (s542).  Same on the base 24988e35 and on s540c`s tree: it is the residue of ns-escaping-filehandle (#2006), not a regression -- but `undef $fh` is how perl programs SAY "close this now", so it is the one place where the program has told us.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | PCL, main 0df490cf):
  my $f = "/tmp/u1.txt"; sub mk { open my $fh, ">", $f or die; $fh }  sub size { -s $f // 0 }
  { my $fh = mk(); print $fh "hello";  undef $fh;    print size(), "\n"; }   # perl 5 | PCL 0
  { my $fh = mk(); print $fh "hello!"; $fh = undef;  print size(), "\n"; }   # perl 6 | PCL 0
  { open my $fh, ">", $f or die; print $fh "local77"; undef $fh; print size(), "\n"; }   # 7 | 7  (opened here: the #1469 licence emits the close ahead of the statement)
  { my %h; $h{fh} = mk(); print { $h{fh} } "inhash88"; delete $h{fh}; print size(), "\n"; }   # 8 | 0
  { my $o = bless { fh => mk() }, "Obj"; print { $o->{fh} } "object1010"; undef $o; print size(), "\n"; }   # 10 | 0

WHY NOT A CLOSE: the variable may not hold the last reference (no reference counts), so closing is wrong when another holder exists.
WHAT IS SAFE: a FLUSH.  Writing the buffered bytes early is invisible to every other holder (perl would write them at the latest at close; a reader of the file sees them sooner, never wrongly).  So: the literal statements `undef $x;` and `$x = undef;` (the two shapes DECIDED line "A condition-`my` handle closes ..." already recognises for a handle opened in the block) emit, for a scalar NOT under the opened-here licence, a run-time "if the old value is a filehandle, finish-output it" before the write.  Cost: one type test at an `undef` statement, nothing on an ordinary assignment (the shape is decided at compile time; `box-set` is not touched).  The first two rows then answer 5 and 6.
NOT COVERED by this (stay with #2006 / the DESTROY design): the hash-element delete and the object holding the handle -- no statement names the handle there.

BAR: the reproducer`s rows 1-2 = perl; a guard in Pl/t/fh-collect-01.t (perl-probed); bench `fhprint` / `cfor` unmoved; the lock is NOT released by the flush (say so in not-supported.md: `undef $fh` on an escaped LOCKED handle still holds the lock until a trigger).

=== DONE (s543b) ===
Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16, WIP f014f5e2.  FIX (Pl emission + cl): the statement shapes the scope-close licence already reads
(`undef $x;`, `undef($x);`, `$x = undef;`) on any other lexical scalar are preceded by (p-flush-dropped-handle $x):
when the OLD value is an open output fd-stream above fd 2 its buffer is WRITTEN -- never a close (another holder may
exist).  One shape reader (_fh_drop_stmt_name) for the close and the flush; the box is peeked, never FETCHed through a
tie.  Probe p6/undef.pl, 15 shapes: rows 1 2 7 13 14 = perl (were 0); `delete $h{fh}` and an object holding the handle
not covered (as the task said); a second holder sees the bytes early (documented); row 11 is #2006's stale buffer
(base wrong too).  Cost: 10M `undef` statements 0.370 -> 0.379 s min (+~1 ns each, load ~10, inside noise).  Guard
Pl/t/fh-collect-01.t row 7 (fails on c5f618f2).  Path-Tiny rows 40-47 stay: the handle a method RETURNED is let go at a
block exit, which no `undef $fh` statement marks (ns-escaping-filehandle, sentence added).


=== NARROWED at MAIN-READY-100 `64353611` (the reviewing session, 2026-11-21; s543b member 6): `undef $fh;` / `undef($fh);` / `$fh = undef;` on a LEXICAL SCALAR of the statement`s own unit now flush an escaped output handle (p-flush-dropped-handle; guard Pl/t/fh-collect-01.t row 7; a flush, never a close; a tied scalar is not FETCHed).  STILL OPEN HERE: `delete $h{fh}` and `undef $obj` where the object holds the handle (this task`s shapes 4 and 5).  Siblings filed: #5128 (the same statements inside a sub on a CAPTURED file-level lexical), #5160 (an IO::File object: the value is a glob handle, not the stream).  The scope-exit shapes are the documented MOMENT limit (ns-escaping-filehandle, #2006 / #2370).

=== s543r (2026-11-21, the round on 64353611) === EIGHT BOARD ROWS wait on this task`s `undef $obj` shape: Pod-Simple htmlbat.t 1-8 (Pod::Simple::HTMLBatch writes each page through a handle held by an object and drops it with `undef($page)`; the test reads the file back at once: perl 25 bytes, main 0 -- probes/objfh.pl in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/round).  Keyed `NS:ns-escaping-filehandle`; a flush that reaches a handle held one level inside the dropped value would take them out.

=== DONE (s543g) ===
Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22.  Shapes 4 and 5: `delete $h{K};` / `delete $r->{K};` (and `$a[I]`) as a whole void statement is wrapped (p-flush-dropped-value (p-delete ...)) -- Pl::Stmt::expr_shape's drop_delete + Parser2::_lower_expr_stmt; the delete's OWN value, read once (a tied hash's DELETE runs once, no FETCH); and the flush's dispatch walks a dropped HASH or ARRAY one level: each of its first +P-FLUSH-WALK-LIMIT+ = 64 direct elements as a handle (stream / glob / fdopen alias), never deeper, never through a tie.  Probes scratch/s543g/probes (the s543g worktree)/m7: delete + undef $obj / $obj = undef on hash, array, blessed, IO::File holders = perl (base 0); two levels down not reached (by design, documented); a second holder sees the bytes early; a lock is not released by the flush.  Pod-Simple t/htmlbat.t one-file 5 / 13 -> 13 / 13 (its rows 1-8 left baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv by edit); Path-Tiny t/input_output.t rows 40-47 still fail on both (the block-exit moment: a method's returned handle let go at `}`, no statement says so).  Guard Pl/t/fh-collect-01.t row 10.  ir-spec 6.5b, not-supported ns-escaping-filehandle.  Cost: see the session log (bench leg).
subject: SILENT WRONG (residue of s543b): `delete $h{fh}` and `undef $obj` (an object holding the handle) of an output handle that ESCAPED its opening block write nothing -- the read-back idiom sees a short file; the plain `undef $fh` / `$fh = undef` statements are fixed
